title: Why does kinetic energy increase quadratically, not linearly, with speed? (2011)
summary: A foundational physics Q&A explaining why kinetic energy follows the quadratic relationship KE = ½mv² rather than linear scaling with velocity, typically using the work-energy theorem and integration of force over distance.
problem_solved: Explains the mathematical and physical origin of the quadratic kinetic energy-velocity relationship in classical mechanics.
why_valuable: Clarifies a fundamental concept in physics education that many students find counterintuitive, with 240 points and 115 comments indicating strong community engagement.
